title: Directed subobject unions pull back to the source of a factoring map
statement: In a Grothendieck abelian category C [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let S_i be a nonempty small directed family of subobjects of Y. If f:X→Y factors through their supremum, then the supremum of the inverse-image subobjects f⁻¹(S_i) is top in Subobject X.

source.place: Tag 079A (section-grothendieck-conditions), AB5 exactness of filtered colimits; directed-intersection distributivity is already proved in the source library

proof.text: For a monomorphism f, push each inverse image forward to im(f)∩S_i and use the proved library lemma IsGrothendieckAbelian.inf_iSup_of_directed in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.Subobject. The factoring assumption makes im(f)∩sup_i S_i equal im(f); injectivity of subobject pushforward along a mono gives the result.

For an epimorphism f and sup_i S_i=top, let U be the union of the inverse images. It contains ker(f), since the family is nonempty, and its image under f is top, because image pushforward preserves suprema and epis are stable under pullback. The cokernel of U descends through f. Its composite with the image of U is zero, so that descended map vanishes, making the cokernel of U zero. Hence U=top.

Factor a general f as an epi onto its image followed by a mono. Apply the mono case to the original family and then the epi case to the resulting family of inverse images. Pullback along a composite finishes the proof.
